title: Research by Vijay: Gmail Auto-Reply Systems
query: "Hey guys! Can someone show me how to build a Gmail auto-reply system that triggers based on the subject line of an email?"
content:
Hey! We built a Gmail auto-reply tool for our internal purpose recently, and we made a few mistakes along the way. So, please avoid those and follow this guide instead.

Initial Setup

First, you need to set up the basics. Get your Gmail API keys from Google Cloud and keep them hidden in your environment variables. Then, build a simple UI where you can type in the keywords you want your tool to look for.

Backend Logic

Next comes the backend logic. Write a Python script that checks your inbox every 5 minutes. When an email comes in, your code should read the subject line and compare it to your keywords.

Mistakes to Avoid

This is where our mistakes started. Our tool replied to an 'Out of Office' message, which replied back, causing an endless loop! To stop this, you have to use Thread Saving. Every time you send a reply, take the Thread ID and store it in the database. So every time while it is replying to a mail, it will check the database. If the Thread ID is there, then it won't reply.

Deployment

Finally, for hosting, use a platform like Render paired with a Neon database. Just remember to use UptimeRobot so your free server doesn't go to sleep. That's it!

title: Research by Vivek: AI-Powered WhatsApp Automation
query: "I run a busy bakery business and get way too many WhatsApp messages every day. Is there a way to build a simple AI that understands my products and replies to customers automatically?"
content:
Hello! Automating WhatsApp is incredibly useful for small businesses, but it is also the easiest way to get your number banned. A friend of ours recently built this project for a small restaurant, so our team researched their setup to show you exactly how to do it safely.

Keep the AI Simple

You don't need a huge database to give the AI knowledge about your business. Just create a simple text file with your menu, prices, and operating hours. Then, use a fast API like Groq. When a customer asks a question, your code just sends their message along with your text file to Groq, and it figures out the perfect answer.

Use the Official Meta API

To actually send the messages, you must use the official Meta WhatsApp Cloud API. Do not use unofficial web-scraping libraries, or Meta will permanently ban your number. Go to the Meta Developer Dashboard, register your app, and get your official access tokens. This keeps your connection 100% legal and stable.

The Spam Filter Problem

Here is the biggest mistake people make: they let the AI reply instantly. When our friend first built this, the tool replied to customers in zero seconds. Even on the official API, sending messages too fast can trigger spam filters. You must add a simple delay in your code. Making the tool wait 4 or 5 seconds before replying makes it look natural.

title: Research by Vardhan: Cracking the TCS NQT Exam
query: "Can someone help me out? I'm taking the TCS NQT next month. I need a solid strategy to crack the coding and aptitude sections since I heard the platform is super weird."
content:
Hi! We just helped a few students prepare for the NQT last week. Their coding logic was actually fine, but they kept failing because they didn't know how the TCS website takes text from the user. It is very different from normal practice sites. Here is what we told them to fix it.

Handling Raw Inputs

This is the main reason people fail. The TCS compiler doesn't give you clean arrays. It just gives you raw text. If you are using Python, you have to get used to typing list(map(int, input().split())). If you use Java, you need to use the Scanner class. Also, one student failed simply because they wrote input("Enter number: ")—if you put any text inside your input prompt, the automated tester will crash immediately.

Don't Ignore the Math

A lot of people spend all their time on LeetCode, but the aptitude section is what actually filters most students out. We told our students to spend a solid week just doing Percentages, Profit & Loss, and Time & Work problems. The math section is just as important as the coding.

Write Simple Scripts for Partial Marks

We saw some students leaving the hard coding questions completely blank. Don't do this. The TCS platform gives you partial marks. Even if you don't know the full logic, just write a basic script that passes the easiest test cases. Getting those 2 or 3 partial marks is usually what gets you the interview call.

title: Research by Vijay: SaaS Customer Churn Prediction
query: "Hello! I run a small SaaS startup. We are getting new users, but a lot of them cancel after the first two months. I want to build a machine learning model to predict who is going to cancel so we can reach out to them first. How do I start building this?"
content:
Hi! Predicting churn is actually super common for SaaS startups. We recently helped a startup that was struggling with the exact same issue for their inventory software. Here is what we learned while building their prediction system.

The Data Imbalance Problem

When we looked at their database, only about 15% of their users had cancelled. If you train an AI on that, it will just guess that 'everyone stays' and look perfectly accurate! To fix this, we used a Python technique called SMOTE. It generates fake examples of cancelled users so your training data is perfectly balanced.

Watch Out for Pipeline Skew

Another big headache we ran into was Training-Serving Skew. You have to save your data-cleaning rules into one file and your trained model into another. If your live web app doesn't clean new user data exactly the same way you cleaned your historical data, the whole system just breaks.

Keep Hosting Simple

We didn't want them paying for expensive cloud servers just to run one model. We wrapped the Python code in a Docker container and deployed it on Render. Now, whenever a new user signs up, the live app just pings the container to check their churn risk, and it costs almost nothing.

title: Research by Vijay: LinkedIn Top Voice Strategy
query: "Does anyone know the exact roadmap to get the LinkedIn Top Voice blue badge for AI? I know it's invite-only, but what should I post daily to actually get the editorial team's attention?"
content:
Honestly, getting the blue badge is a popularity contest first. The editors do not search for random people; they only look at accounts that are already going viral. You have to get regular users to comment on your posts first.

Stop Posting AI Prompts

Nobody cares about generic ChatGPT prompt lists anymore. If you want real engagement, post deep-dives into actual code or architectures. The LinkedIn algorithm only pushes your post if people actually start debating in the comments.

Clean Up Your Profile

Once you finally go viral, an editor will eventually check your page. Drop the 'AI Enthusiast' headline. Just say exactly what you build, and link your GitHub right at the top. If they see viral posts backed up by a real developer profile, that's when you get the invite.

title: Research by Charan: Completely Private Local AI
query: "Quick question: My company handles sensitive financial data, so we legally cannot send data to OpenAI's servers. How do we build a completely private AI chatbot that runs locally on our own office machines?"
content:
Hey! This is a really common problem for finance and healthcare teams. You definitely do not need to send your data to the cloud. We recently helped a local clinic set up an offline AI on their office computer, and it is actually pretty straightforward if you use the right tools.

Skip the Python Scripts, Use Ollama

Trying to build a local server from scratch with Python usually ends in a mess of dependency errors. Instead, just install Ollama. It works a bit like Docker but it is built specifically for running AI models locally. You just download it, open your terminal, and type ollama run llama3. That's it, the server is running offline.

Give Your Team a Normal UI

Your finance team is not going to want to type questions into a black terminal window. To fix this, you should install Open WebUI. It connects directly to Ollama running on your machine and gives you a clean interface that looks exactly like ChatGPT. It even runs on your local network, so anyone in the office can open their browser and use it.

Read Your Own Documents Securely

The best part about Open WebUI is that it has a built-in document reader (RAG). Your team can drag and drop their sensitive PDFs straight into the chat window. The documents are processed entirely on your local hard drive, so the AI can answer questions about your financial records without a single byte of data ever leaving your laptop.

title: Research by Charan: Automated Faceless YouTube Shorts
query: "I want to build a faceless YouTube Shorts channel for historical facts. How can I automate the entire pipeline from script generation to video editing and uploading, without getting shadowbanned by the algorithm for spam?"
content:
Automating a channel is totally possible, but YouTube is very aggressive about banning bot farms. We recently set up a workflow for a faceless channel, and we figured out how to avoid getting flagged.

Stop using standard AI voices

Do not use the default TikTok or Google text-to-speech voices. YouTube recognizes them instantly and will restrict your views. You need to use something like the ElevenLabs API. If you use a custom cloned voice, the algorithm usually registers it as human.

The Automation Stack

Most people try to use Zapier to connect everything, but it gets way too expensive for heavy video files. We used Make.com instead. You can set it up to grab a daily script from the Groq API, send that text to ElevenLabs for the voiceover, and then push the audio to an API like Creatomate. Creatomate automatically slaps on stock footage and captions and gives you a finished MP4.

Don't fully automate the upload

If a bot pushes videos live at the exact same time every day, YouTube will flag you. Instead, just set the API to upload the videos as 'Private'. Then, open the YouTube app on your phone, check if the video looks good, and publish it manually. It keeps the account safe.

title: Research by Vivek: AI Lead Scoring in Google Sheets
query: "Hey team, I run a marketing agency and we get hundreds of lead inquiries dumped into a Google Sheet. It takes hours to read them. How can we integrate AI directly into Google Sheets to instantly read and score these leads for us?"
content:
We recently set this up for an agency that was wasting hours reading junk leads every morning. You definitely do not need to pay for Zapier to do this. You can actually build the AI directly into your spreadsheet.

Use Apps Script, not Zapier

Instead of using expensive third-party tools, just use Google Apps Script. It is built right into Sheets. You can write a small JavaScript function that takes the text from your lead column, sends it to an API like OpenAI, and spits a score from 1 to 10 back into the next column. It basically lets you type =SCORE_LEAD(A2) just like a normal SUM formula.

Watch out for timeouts

Here is the main issue we ran into: Google Sheets will crash your formula and show an error if the API takes longer than 30 seconds to reply. To fix this, do not drag the formula down 500 rows at once. Instead, set up an onEdit trigger in the code. That way, the AI only runs in the background when a brand new row is added.

Automate the next step

Once the scoring is working, the easiest way to speed up your workflow is Conditional Formatting. Set any row with a score of 8 or higher to turn green. That way, your sales team can instantly see who the hot leads are without reading a single message.

title: Research by Vijay: Self-Hosted AI Attendance & Payroll System
query: "I'm a Jr Python developer and I run a small business. I don't want to pay for Keka or third-party HR tools anymore. How can I build a simple, self-hosted facial recognition system that only marks attendance when employees are physically in the office, and also generates their payslips?"
content:
We actually built something very similar recently. The biggest mistake people make is trying to process the live video feed directly on the backend. It will crash your server instantly.

Process the face on the frontend

The trick is to use a library like face-api.js directly in the browser. It calculates the math behind the face locally on the employee's phone. Then, the frontend just sends a tiny string of numbers to your Django backend instead of heavy video files.

Use a Vector Database

A normal SQL database cannot compare faces. We used Neon PostgreSQL because it supports pgvector natively. When someone logs in, the database compares the new face math to the saved one. If the distance is under 0.5, it marks them as present.

Stop them from logging in at home

To make sure they are actually in the office, you have to use a Geofence. We set it up so the frontend grabs their GPS coordinates using the Google Maps API. Before Django even checks the face, it verifies if their GPS coordinates are inside a 4-point digital box drawn around the office. If they are outside the box, it rejects the login immediately.

Automate the Payslips

Because you own the raw attendance data now, generating payslips is easy. You just need to set up a monthly cron job in your Django backend. Have the script calculate their net pay by subtracting any absent days from their base salary. Then, use a Python library like WeasyPrint to convert a basic HTML payslip template into a PDF, and automatically email it out using the Gmail API.
